quick_english: Now the glad-hearted should go to the worship-place; for wherever the heart is gladdened, fit for absorption into the Lord, it becomes — that alone, not anything else is the mark: even at the saying, meditated-identity alone is the cause; that too is from being-glad alone — nothing else is the place.
But seat-mountain-top and the rest in scripture is to be understood as aimed at this place-pointing.

In these seats and the rest, by the Lord's ordainment, of powers entered by the Lord taking body — like noble lands for the pious, like barbarian lands for the impious; the mountain-top teaching from solitude, from distraction-avoidance, is one-pointed-state — thus.
There before the worship-house, outside alone, one should do the general placing — first on hands, then on the body.

hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ, hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ — thus; by these two, expressing power and power-bearer, the two Mālinī-alphabet mantras; with one alone, first power, then power-bearer — thus; in release from foot-tip to head-ending; in enjoyment all is reversed.
For Mālinī the Goddess is the chief Śākta form, all-wish-milking through seed-womb collision.

And meaningful is this name: garlanded with Rudra-power garlands, flowering in fruits, the winter-dissolving-sound bee, holding attainment-release, endowed with giving-taking power — thus from oneness-remembering of ra and la.
Hence very, for even a broken-rite mantra becomes complete through this placing; even a stained Gāruḍa-Vaiṣṇava and the rest, having reached stainlessness, becomes release-giving.
After body-placing, this same placing is for the vessel.

For here, for firmness of realization of non-difference with the Lord, the worship-act is made example: there, of all factors, thus is the Lord-ness of the Lord; there, from sacrificer-support's place-purity-bringing-doings, from vessel-purity-placing, from sacrificer's body-placing, from worshippable's altar-placing.
Thus, even by rite-order alone, making all factors the Lord's, seeing all rites with just this view, without chief knowledge and yoga — one becomes the Supreme Lord.
Thus having placed on the vessel, having worshipped with flowers, smoke and the rest, one should sprinkle the rite-essence and flowers and the rest with its drops.
Then in the halo-circle, on ground or in sky: oṃ to the outer retinue, hail — thus one should worship.
Then at the door-place: oṃ to the door-deity-wheel, hail — thus one should worship.
But if there is an unguarded outer place, having entered, on the maṇḍala-altar-front alone the outer-retinue-door-deity-wheel worship, the aforesaid placing and the rest one should do — not outside.

Then too: phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ — thus, having thrown the weapon-muttered flower, having removed obstacles, having meditated, having entered within, with gaze kindled by the Lord's ray, one should see all around the worship-house.
There the release-seeker should stand facing north, so that by the Lord's Aghora-radiance swiftly indeed, burnt-bonded, he may become.
There the Lord's freedom alone, by form-shining, shines forth the direction-principle.

There awareness-light alone is the middle; thence other-division-arising: to be taken as light is above, what is not thus is below; facing light is east, the other west; from being become-facing-light, the next is that-light-stream-rise-place; south from favour; facing it, but from to-be-shone, north — thus the direction-four.

There in the middle the Lord; above his is the north-eastern face; below the underworld face; in the east-and-rest four directions the one called Tatpuruṣa-Aghora-Sadyas-Vāma; in the four-direction-middle the other four.
Thus indeed awareness-glory alone forms direction-difference as form — thus direction is not another principle.
As, as the shadow is to be overstepped — being, before, before, it becomes — so reaching the Lord's centrality: being all-presiding alone is centrality — thus it is said.

Thus as the Lord is the divider of directions, so the sun — for it indeed is the Lord's knowledge-power — thus said: there, there, there the east is of the manifest from the east; and just where, so there — thus self-ruled even, facing one's own place, is in front.
Thus by self-sun-Lord-triad-unification is direction-discussion — thus Abhinavagupta's gurus.

Thus standing, facing north one should sit, in body-city-eight and the rest by I-feeling abandonment; body-ness one should burn; from nearness too as another's body, from bodilessness — then mounted on the waveless steady abode, from gaze-nature — which indeed is the first throb-digit — that alone is the form; thereupon is the as-taught worshippable-deity-wheel-placing; chiefly too here the powers are to be worshipped.
From being that seat, and of the Lord-nine-self and the rest, of power alone and of worship-worthiness — thus the gurus.
There five states: waking and the rest; and sixth, called unsurpassed, is the nature-state to be contemplated.
Thus sixfold is the placing.

There, from the presiding of causes — Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra-Īśa-Sadāśiva-power-formed — each, from thirty-six-principle-group's world-transcended, in Bhairavabhaṭṭāraka-non-difference-course, placing, from fullness, is Bhairavī-being; hence this has no opening.
Which, they said: gained in waveless mounting, again what — is category-emission through placing and the rest — thus.
So long indeed that waveless Bhairava-formed which shows in own self emission-dissolution-variety-peak.
Thus the mutually-meeting-yoga-made Lord's own breath-body-mind, having contemplated, outside and within with flowers-smoke-satings and the rest as possible, one should worship.

There in the body, in breath, in mind and accordingly one should do the trident-lotus-placing — as at base-power-root: root, bulb, to root-pith, at the hanging-end, to kalā-principle's end the staff; Māyā-natured knot; fourfold-natured pure-knowledge lotus; right there the Lord Sadāśiva; he alone the great corpse, through excellence, from dissolved-ness, from awakening, chiefly; from knowable-bodied body-decay, from sound-touch-awareness-nature and the rest.

That risen from the navel, come out of the three head-openings at its top, abiding inside sound, power-pervader, equanimity-formed and the rest, the six-end; thereupon is the pure lotus-triad, beyond-mind; on this universe-made division made seat, presiding as pervading-being, the desired become-supported deity having fashioned — which right there, in same-disposition-full self, universe-being-offering: that alone is worship; which alone becoming-that: that is meditation; which inner-deliberation-being-shaking as of such: that is murmur; which by such-deliberation-order-awakened great-splendour, by that force alone, is universe-self-making: that is oblation; that very thing done thus, the retinue, from that alone, from fire-heap like sparks, having meditated, just so one should worship.
Remembering the twelve-end, the foremost, the trident, from the root.
Leaving sequence, going to the goddess-wheel-front attains sky-going-ness.
From the root-support, to the twice-six-end-sky-peak-filling-natured.
Of sky-going-ness, from sky-faring-rest and from sky-nectar-eating.
Thus by inner-rite alone in reality is done-what-was-to-be-done.

Truly for the then-entered, still outer is to be done, the rite, to remove limitation alone — who too thus does not partake immersion: his chief is the outer rite; from its practice, immersion-gain; since of him too, but the beast-veiling inner rite, when mounted on that too, of his thought-force is purity-giving.
Now when one wishes to do initiation: for the sake of that-days preparation, ground-taking, Gaṇeśa-worship, jar-and-vessel worship, altar-worship, oblation one should do.
But in daily-and-occasional, altar-and-rest worship-oblation alone.
There is initiation-preparation, the disciple's refined-fitness-placing, like sharpening as it were of teeth; the God's toward-work-upturned-ness-grasping, the guru's taking of that.
By being inside the worship-house, the implement-things, through the Lord's radiance-swelling, is bestowing of worship-implement-fitness — thus.

There, having arranged the worship-house full of all implements, having remembered the Goddess Mālinī or Mātṛkā, bearing the taken, full of her-letter-radiance-mass, one should cast the flower-handful.
Then having scattered as possible stated weapon-muttered mustard-grain-parched-rice and the rest, radiance-formed, gathering in order in the north-east — thus is ground-taking.

Then having given the seat up to pure-knowledge's end, Gaṇeśa's worship; then having filled the jar, filled with bliss-substance, adorned, one should worship; then the worshippable next, betel, having placed, there the chief mantra, as all-presiding, remembering with rule-precedence, with that 108-times-muttered, that jar one should make.
In the second vessel, weapons for quelling obstacles one should worship.
Then in own directions the world-guardians with weapons one should worship.
Then to the before-initiated disciple's hand one should give the weapon-vessel.
And oneself the guru should take the jar.

Then making the disciple pour the stream around the house for obstacle-quelling, with jar the guru should follow him, reciting this mantra: O, O Indra! by you in your own direction for obstacle-pacifying.
With attentiveness, to be done at rite's end, by Śiva's command.
In the three-syllabled name, O is one alone — thus.
Then in the north-east direction one should place the jar.
Upon the scattered, the weapon-vessel.
Then the worship of both.
Then in the altar-middle is Supreme-worship.

Then having contemplated the fire-pit as Supreme-power-formed, having kindled fire there, having made one with heart-inner-awakening-fire, with mantra-deliberation-accompaniment, contemplating the blazing Śiva-fire, having placed there, having worshipped, one should sate the mantras with ghee and sesame.
And with the vessel, sprinkling alone: of sesame-ghee and the rest, refining.
And of ladle-and-spoon non-difference-view alone indeed is refining.

Then having offered as able, having arranged ladle-and-spoon up-down-facing as power-and-Śiva-formed, mutually facing, having stood with even feet, contemplating the stream of supreme nectar fallen, risen in the sky of the twelve-end, risen full-Śiva-moon, and uttering the mantra ending in vauṣaḍ, until ghee's end one should stand — thus the full oblation, mantra-wheel-sating.
Then having brought the sprinkled caru, on altar-vessel-jar-fires offering share by share, having left one share over, to the disciple one should give a share.
Then the tooth-stick.
Its falling in fire-Yama-Nirṛti directions and below is not auspicious — thus.
There oblation by weapon-mantra is to be done.
Then for distraction-avoidance, for fitness to see the future mantra, having made the blindfolded disciple enter, having made him kneeling, one should have him cast a flower-handful.

Then suddenly, unfastened-eye-bound, he — through descent-graced instrument-ness, seeing the present mantra in that place face-to-face, becomes made of that; of graced instruments the mantra-nearness is visible, since as it were of trembling beings.
Then having worshipped the deity-wheel with blazing in one's own right hand, placing it — burning the disciple's bonds on head-heart-navel — one should place down.
Then in the left with gentleness, having worshipped, fattening with pure-principle — then one should bow.
Then the being-deity-direction-offering, full of wine-meat-water and the rest, outside one should give; having sipped.
Then having eaten the oblation-meal oneself, with the disciple-self attaining oneness, awakened-natured one should stay.
Dreaming too, at dawn if the disciple tells an inauspicious dream — that to him one should not explain.
For doubt and fear would be his; merely with the weapon one should make its expiation.

Then just so having worshipped the Lord, having entered before him by the disciple's breath-course, touching the six-cause-touching in the heart-throat-palate-brow-cleft-twelve-ends, each eight refinements contemplating, some time resting the disciple-breath right there, again one should descend.
Thus effected-forty-eight-refinements-upon-made-Rudra-part-attainment becomes a samayin.
Then to him the worshippable mantra with flowers and the rest one should bestow.
Then the rules to him one should lay down.

In the guru with whole self, devotion; so in scripture; in God; aversion toward their opponents; like the guru, of the guru's son and the rest; of the knowledge-tied made, of the before-initiated and the rest, seeing; of the womb-tie, for its honouring, not by oneself — thus to be deemed.
Of women, of the barren the cause of that-loathing one should not do.
Deity-name, guru-name, and mantra, apart from worship-time one should not utter.
What the guru has enjoyed — bed and the rest — one should not enjoy.
What games and the rest are worldly, that in the guru's nearness one should not do.
Apart from that, elsewhere one should not make excellence-thought.
Everywhere, in śrāddha and the rest, the guru alone one should worship.
And in all occasionals, śākinī and the rest, words one should not say.
Festival days one should worship.
With those of lower sight, Vaiṣṇavas and the rest, company one should not make.
Abiding in this teaching, one should not see with former-birth thought.
When the guru's circle has come home, as able one should do worship.
A lower-path abider, a Vaiṣṇava and the rest, having even made him guru, from his teaching-clan, one should abandon.
Even then one should not see with excellence-thought.
With mark-bearers no conduct-meeting one should make; them only as able one should worship.
Doubts one should abandon.
In the wheel, standing, of last-and-first division, birth-made, one should not fancy.
Apart from the body, apart from, no other abode-ford and the rest with high regard one should see.

Constantly one should remember the mantra-heart — thus, so the disciple, having heard, having bowed, having accepted, the guru with wealth-wife-body-up-to gift having pleased, the before-initiated and poor-lordless and the rest sating.
And with the future rule, the image-wheel one should sate.
Thus one becomes a samayin.
In mantra-practice, in daily worship, in hearing, in study, entitled; but in the occasional, everywhere the guru alone one should request.
Thus the samayin rule.
